note: Set A's nine claims are all accurate and correctly bound, but it repeats the HabEx starshade diameter three times and omits several facts on the page (LUVOIR-A 15 m aperture, LUVOIR-B's three instruments, Origins 5.9 m and its three instruments, HabEx's four instruments). Set B covers more of the page but contains many misbound and garbled claims: instrument counts attached to generic 'on-axis/off-axis/axis telescope', 'spacecraft' or the Lynx mirror assembly instead of the mission concepts, the 10 m focal length reported as a mirror-assembly 'dimension' and even as a 'diameter', and a truncated 'n-axis telescope' entity. B also repeats the LUVOIR-B, HabEx and starshade facts several times under slightly different names. A is clearly the better set despite its gaps.
remarks: Both sets miss Origins entirely in A and only partially in B (B has the 5.9 m aperture but not its three science instruments). B's quotes show text-layer truncation artifacts ('n-axis telescope', '10 m nd three science instruments', 'grazing incidence mir'), suggesting the extractor split on hyphens and line breaks; entity resolution should map generic telescope/mirror/spacecraft phrases back to the mission-concept bullet they belong to.
